speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the rash on your scalp and forehead, specifically regarding its appearance and any associated symptoms like itching or pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash extend into the ear canals, eyebrows, or nasolabial folds, and have you noticed any crusting or oozing from the affected areas? I would like to examine the distribution of the lesions to distinguish between seborrheic dermatitis and atopic dermatitis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any significant itching or discomfort from the rash, and does it tend to flare up during times of stress? I am trying to differentiate between seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis based on symptom severity and triggers.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the age of the patient and the presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, this presentation is classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis, also known as cradle cap. I do not require further testing as the clinical picture is distinct from psoriasis or atopic dermatitis in this age group. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis
